title: Introducing Sphinx Browser Agents: AI Analysts Inside Your Tools
summary: Sphinx Browser Agents log into the compliance tools you already use and work cases inside them. Onboarded with a username and password, no integration project.
body_markdown:
Today we're launching Sphinx Browser Agents, AI analysts that log into the compliance tools you already run and work cases inside them, with no integration project on your side.


Compliance tooling is fragmented. Case management lives in one system, transaction monitoring in another, screening somewhere else, and a layer of internal tools holds it all together. Getting any of it to talk to each other is complicated. And compliance is rarely engineering's top priority, so even when the APIs exist, the integration sits in a backlog. Meanwhile the alerts keep arriving. Here's what we built to work around that.


## Integration was never an engineering problem


Here's a conversation we have over and over. A compliance team wants to automate alert review. Their screening vendor has an API. Their case management system has an API. Everyone agrees it should be possible. Then the ticket goes to engineering, lands behind the product roadmap, and a quarter later the team is still[working the queue by hand](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/why-are-screening-alerts-piling-up) .


The gap was never technical. It's a question of whose time gets spent. Compliance doesn't ship revenue, so it waits.


The industry's answers all assume that time will show up eventually. Platform migrations promise one system that does everything, after a year of implementation. Middleware promises to connect what you have, once engineering configures it. Each one asks someone to build something before a single alert gets cleared.


We took a different approach. A new analyst doesn't need an API. They get a login.


## How it works


Sphinx works directly across your systems using browser agents. You onboard an agent the way you'd onboard a person, and it operates inside your tools the way a person would: same screens, same clicks, same case notes.


Browser agents produce work and recommendations. They don't change your systems, your policies, or who signs off. Which queues the agent handles, and how far it goes before a person steps in, is up to you.


## What this looks like in production


This is how Sphinx has connected to customer systems from the start.[Conduit](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/conduit-dispositions-risk-alerts-99-faster-with-sphinx) connected Sphinx to its transaction monitoring and analytics tools with a standard username and password, then cleared a backlog that would have taken six months by hand in two days.[Morse](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-morse-saves-200-hours-on-monthly-alert-reviews-with-sphinx) pointed Sphinx at its screening alerts and now resolves sanctions hits at roughly 99.9% precision, saving the FinCrime team about 200 hours a month.


Neither team migrated a system. Neither team pulled in engineering. The agent got a login, learned the procedures, and started working the queue.


## Built for scrutiny


An agent that clicks through your systems has to be at least as accountable as the analyst it works beside. So every case a Sphinx agent touches is traceable: the screens it visited, the data it pulled, the sources it checked, the procedure it applied, and the recommendation it made. The analyst sees all of it in the extension before they act, and the record stays with the case.


When an examiner asks how a decision was made six months ago, you can show the exact evidence the agent reviewed, the reasoning it gave, the analyst who approved it, and every update to the procedure since. That's the standard our[Interpretable Agentic Framework](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-sphinx-makes-every-decision-auditable---the-interpretable-agentic-framework) was built to, and browser agents inherit it.


## Why we built it


Every deployment used to start with the same negotiation: which systems can we integrate, how long will it take, and who on the customer's side will do the work. The answer was always some version of "later." Compliance teams were ready. Their engineering calendars weren't.


The browser is the one interface every compliance tool already has. Agents that use it the way analysts do let us start where the work is instead of waiting on a backlog.


## See Sphinx Browser Agents in action


The fastest way to see what this looks like is to give Sphinx a login to one queue you're already behind on.


It's live today and works on top of the systems you already use. Keep what you have. No retraining for the compliance team, no pulling in engineering, just humans and agents working side by side.


If you're a BSA Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Financial Crime, or you run compliance operations at a bank, payments company, or fintech, we'll connect Sphinx to your tools and show you it working your real cases.


– Alex & Chris
